strands.title: Strands Agents — Open Source AI Agent SDK for Python & TypeScript
strands.summary: Strands Agents is an open source SDK for building production agents with tools, MCP integration, model providers, guardrails, observability, and deployment paths.

selected_docs.title: Quickstart: Python
selected_docs.description: Get an AI agent running in Python in under 5 minutes. Install the SDK, configure a model provider, and build your first agent.

selected_docs.title: Using MCP Tools
selected_docs.description: Connect AI agents to any MCP server for tool access. Strands agents integrate and invoke MCP tools without custom integration code.

selected_docs.title: amazon-bedrock
selected_docs.description: Use Amazon Bedrock models in Strands agents. Configure AWS credentials, model settings, guardrails, prompt caching, and multi-modal input.

selected_docs.title: operating-agents-in-production
selected_docs.description: Deploy AI agents to production on AWS Lambda, EKS, Fargate, EC2, or Bedrock AgentCore. Monitoring, scaling, and operational best practices.

selected_docs.title: deploy_to_bedrock_agentcore
selected_docs.description: Deploy Strands agents to Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Runtime: a serverless, session-isolated platform that scales agents without managing servers.

selected_docs.title: responsible-ai
selected_docs.description: Build AI agents responsibly with Strands: least-privilege tool design, input validation, audit logging, and ethical deployment practices.

selected_docs.title: guardrails
selected_docs.description: Add safety guardrails to AI agents. Control tool permissions, validate outputs, and enforce responsible AI policies in production.

selected_docs.title: observability
selected_docs.description: Monitor AI agents with OpenTelemetry traces, metrics, and logs. Debug agent behavior and measure performance in production.

selected_docs.title: metrics
selected_docs.description: Track agent performance metrics in Strands: token usage, latency, tool call counts, and event loop cycles, all available through AgentResult.

problem_statements.title: Running more efficient trials
problem_statements.description: Most drugs fail in clinical trials. Learn from previous trials and identify patterns and strategies to design and run better trials in the future.

problem_statements.title: Repurposing opportunities
problem_statements.description: Many different drugs can hit similar targets but running trials for all drug-disease pairs is not practical. Can you identify opportunities for new applications of existing drug based on the progress of other similar drugs?

problem_statements.title: Treatment observability for patients
problem_statements.description: Help patients who are looking for more treatments understand their options. Patients with serious or rare conditions will want to know what cutting edge treatments are available in a clinical trial or maybe approved soon.

problem_statements.title: Claims Adjudication Simulator
problem_statements.description: How might we build an agent that simulates the payer-side prior-authorization/claims adjudication process — reading a prescription and a plan's coverage policy to determine and explain an approve/deny decision in real time, versus today's slow manual review.

problem_statements.title: Reducing Redundant Content Development at Scale
problem_statements.description: Pharma content starts in Regulatory Affairs (white papers, labels, FDA/EMA submissions) and flows downstream to Medical Affairs, MSLs, and Sales — each re-deriving similar content from the same source, duplicating effort and risking inconsistent messaging. Build an AI tool that ingests source content once and automatically repackages it for each downstream audience (tone, depth, format) — while keeping every output traceable back to the single approved source.

candidate_lanes.title: Running more efficient trials
candidate_lanes.fit: Use Strands tools to retrieve prior trial records, normalize endpoints, and produce pattern summaries with traceable sources.

candidate_lanes.title: Repurposing opportunities
candidate_lanes.fit: Use Bright Data or other retrieval tools to collect public drug/target/trial progress evidence, then rank opportunities with source custody.

candidate_lanes.title: Treatment observability for patients
candidate_lanes.fit: Build a patient-facing treatment option monitor that separates trial availability from medical advice.

candidate_lanes.title: Claims Adjudication Simulator
candidate_lanes.fit: Model payer policy reading as a guarded tool workflow with approve/deny rationale and citations.

candidate_lanes.title: Reducing Redundant Content Development at Scale
candidate_lanes.fit: Use Strands agents to transform approved source material into audience-specific outputs while preserving traceability.

openai_agent.output: OpenAI provides advanced language models that can assist in data analysis, natural language processing, and generating insights from biopharma-related datasets in the AWS environment.

reviewers.label: Claim ceiling and rights

findings.finding: The repository and dashboard correctly document a firm claim ceiling ("REPURPOSING_HYPOTHESIS / reproducible evidence workflow only") and list prohibited clinical claims. However, UI text and some agent outputs (e.g. OpenAI agent output: "OpenAI provides advanced language models that can assist...") could be interpreted by non-expert viewers as implying clinical utility if not explicitly framed ev
findings.fix: Add an explicit, persistent UI disclaimer near any model-derived text and the evidence graph: state clearly that outputs are hypothesis-generating only, not clinical recommendations. Ensure any agent output panels include a visible badge: "Not clinical advice — hypotheses only" and avoid language that implies efficacy or treatment recommendation.

findings.finding: Data policy requires 'usage_rights_verified' metadata before publishing provider outputs. The dashboard includes local copies of MagicStudioBox and other provider-derived artifacts and a figure receipt, but snapshot entries do not show per-artifact 'usage_rights_verified' or explicit license/terms fields required by the Data Policy metadata block.
findings.fix: Attach the required metadata to each imported artifact record (public_data, contains_phi, access_restricted, usage_rights_verified, source, source_record_id, dataset_version, license_or_terms, retrieved_at, payload_sha256). Do not publish raw provider outputs until 'usage_rights_verified' is true; redact or summarize provider outputs when redistribution is not permitted.

findings.finding: Chain-of-custody design and receipts are present (Merkle receipt, tamper test, figure receipt) which supports reproducibility. However, some consumer-facing elements (e.g., overnight artifact listings, figure) present derived outputs without inline links to the minimal provenance metadata (who ran the job, command, exact input snapshot timestamps) that audit reviewers may need to reproduce results
findings.fix: Expose concise provenance fields in the dashboard next to each artifact/figure: command run, generator version + commit SHA, exact input file SHAs (already available in figure_receipt.source_files), retrieved_at timestamps and a minimal reproduce command. Link to custody/verify scripts from the UI.

findings.finding: The OpenAI red-team panel intentionally renders an omitted status for the previous red-team output. The developer note says the current OpenAI red-team result is being generated now; omission is intentional and not a failure. Leaving 'omitted_for_current_review' without contextual guidance could confuse viewers about whether red-team review happened.
findings.fix: When red-team output is intentionally omitted, display a short explanatory note in the UI (e.g. 'Red-team review in progress — prior red-team outputs intentionally excluded to avoid self-review. Results will be published when available.'). Ensure final releases include red-team reviewer verdicts and findings inline or as linked artefacts once ready.

findings.finding: Bright Data MCP reports 'token_not_visible' and credential_status 'optional; not visible'. The repo README and status explain tokens are read from environment or .env and not committed. No secrets are included in the snapshot — good practice.
findings.fix: No action required beyond continuing to avoid committing .env and showing the explicit 'not configured' state in the UI. Optionally add a brief UI hint explaining that 'token_not_visible' is expected for demo/local runs and does not indicate a dashboard failure.

reviewers.label: Live dashboard viability

findings.finding: Dashboard rendering relies on ./data/dashboard_snapshot.json. If the snapshot is missing or structure deviates from expected fields (biopharma.candidate_lanes, problem_statements, integrations, overnight, custody, etc.), rendering may throw or sections may be blank.
findings.fix: Ensure the snapshot at data/dashboard_snapshot.json is present and adheres to aws-biopharma.dashboard.v1 schema. Consider adding defensive guards in app.js to handle missing optional fields gracefully (default fallbacks and user-friendly messages).

findings.finding: OpenAI Red Team is omitted_for_current_review in the payload. This is explicitly allowed and not a dashboard failure, but team review should be aware that the red-team surface is not currently rendered.
findings.fix: Document that the red-team surface is intentionally omitted in this snapshot and provide a separate access path or sample rendering in a staging snapshot if needed for reviewer completeness.

findings.finding: Bright Data credential is token_not_visible. The readme notes token aliases may be in environment/.env. This is a visible integration status, not a dashboard failure, and does not block rendering.
findings.fix: No code fix required; consider adding a small status note in the UI explaining that token values are intentionally hidden and how to configure locally if reviewers need to test integration flow.

findings.finding: Run path is explicit in README and the static dashboard is served from public with a local HTTP server on port 8765. If reviewers run in a containerized or CI environment, ensure port exposure and static assets path remain consistent.
findings.fix: If adopting CI/local containers, provide an alternative npm-based serve script or a small dev server config to mirror the README steps in non-CLI environments.

findings.finding: Dashboard surfaces depend on several integrations (OpenAI agent, Bright Data, etc.). The pre-review snapshot indicates some integrations are present but may be partially configured (e.g., AWS_PROFILE/REGION not set in env). The UI shows statuses but some tool access may require additional auth steps to reveal full tool visibility.
findings.fix: Include a short status note in the Integration State panel clarifying required environment configuration for full tool visibility (e.g., MCP clients, MCP tokens).

reviewers.recommended_next_step: Ensure data/dashboard_snapshot.json is present and matches the expected schema referenced by the dashboard JS (biopharma.dashboard.v1). reviewers.label: Secrets and client safety

findings.finding: OPENAI_API_KEY is present in environment/config (per dashboard snapshot); value is not published in code. This is acceptable for local smoke agent, but ensure keys are never committed to the repo and are restricted to the runtime environment.
findings.fix: Do not commit API keys to version control. Store in environment-secured vault or .env consumed at runtime only; audit that build artifacts do not leak keys.

findings.finding: Bright Data token status shows token_not_visible; credential_status is optional and not exposed in the shell. This aligns with the demo’s privacy rules, but keep token management isolated from client-side code.
findings.fix: Maintain token aliases in server-side env or secure MCP config; ensure UI never renders actual tokens or secrets.

findings.finding: Front-end dashboard code fetches local snapshot data and renders UI; no secret tokens are embedded in public JS or HTML paths. OpenAI usage is described as server/local-side via Strands agent, not via browser.
findings.fix: Continue to validate that any provider API calls (OpenAI, Bright Data) originate from server-side components and that the public dashboard only consumes non-secret artifacts.

reviewers.recommended_next_step: Validate that all sensitive credentials (OPENAI_API_KEY, Bright Data tokens) are strictly used server-side and never embedded in client-side bundles. Add a simple legal/tech note to the dashboard to state secrets are kept out of public artifacts.,Perform a quick secret-scan on the repo to confirm no secrets exist in code or snapshots, and add a .gitignore rule for .env files if not already present

reviewers.label: Claim ceiling and rights

findings.finding: Dashboard boundary and prose explicitly reject therapeutic efficacy and clinical utility claims, but the knowledge graph and problem statements could be interpreted as illustrating pathways toward clinical trial design or treatment observability responses. Risk of overclaiming exists if future iterations soften boundaries or add candidate results implying efficacy.
findings.fix: Maintain strict wording around boundary: ensure any future iterations keep the Prohibited / Unsupported Claims section prominent and prevent any visuals or copy that imply treatment efficacy or clinical utility. Include a labeled disclaimer near visualizations that patient-level impact is not claimed.

findings.finding: Evidence shows provider outputs (e.g., Bright Data, Convoke, etc.) are treated as local-only with Redistribution Rights not automatically granted; the dashboard snapshot notes that outputs are not relicensed and rights must be verified. This is correct but relies on reviewer discipline to avoid redistributing raw outputs.
findings.fix: Reinforce on the UI and in documentation that provider outputs are shown only under verified redistribution rights and are not to be published broadly. Add a small footer note in dashboard stating redistribution rights must be verified per provider terms.

findings.finding: Bright Data token is token_not_visible; the status is explicitly shown as optional and not a dashboard failure. This is consistent with the demo design but could invite confusion about access scope if presented to non-technical stakeholders.
findings.fix: Keep token_not_visible status with explicit labelling as optional. Consider a short tooltip clarifying token visibility and that no credentials are exposed in the UI.

findings.finding: OpenAI red-team output is omitted for current review (omitted_for_current_review). This is acceptable per repo guidance and does not block rendering, but it reduces transparency of the red-team posture for teammates.
findings.fix: Document the omission reason in a visible team note (not in secrets) and provide a placeholder status in the UI indicating red-team review is pending or intentionally omitted, to maintain reproducible evidence workflow.

reviewers.recommended_next_step: Preserve and clearly label the dashboard boundary to prevent any inference of clinical efficacy. Maintain the REPURPOSING_HYPOTHESIS / reproducible evidence workflow claim boundary in all future iterations.,Strengthen redistribution-rights governance in UI/documentation: add a concise note about local-use only and rights verification for provider outputs; avoid any redistribution beyond permitted
